Platforms: macOS Apple silicon (signed, notarized dmg/zip with in-app updates); Linux AppImage + deb and Windows exe on releases since 2.3; a headless server and the `realm` CLI ship inside every app at resources/bin from 2.5.0 and run on the app's own binary (no Node); Realm for iPhone (TestFlight)
Supported agents: Claude Code (Agent SDK), Codex (app-server), and Cursor, Gemini, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot, goose, Qwen Code, Grok, fx, DeepSeek, OpenHands, Hermes through one generic ACP adapter; any command line via `realm run` (stub proven here)
Parallelism model: Session per agent, optionally in its own worktree; teammates and sub-agents fanned out from a session across providers (agent_start / delegation); `realm run` launches N commands into N worktrees concurrently
Isolation: Git worktree per session or run under ~/Realm/worktrees, each with a reserved port block exported to its shells; optional per-space macOS Seatbelt sandbox for agents and terminals (not a container; network stays open)
Diff review / merge / PR: Changes pane (diffs grouped by kind), checkpoints with restore, commit + push + open PR as one action (workspace.ship), Code Review page for pull requests through the user's gh with reviewer runs
Remote / mobile / cloud: Strong: a remote runtime, `realm serve --listen`, over TLS, behind Tailscale Serve (`--tailscale`) or through an SSH tunnel, with revocable access tokens (stored hashed, rate-limited, browser origins refused); `--server` aims every `realm` command at it; `realm service install` keeps it running under systemd or launchd; Realm for iPhone pairs with a Mac or a headless server (`realm pair` draws the code in a terminal) through Realm's production relay, end-to-end encrypted. The iPhone app is a TestFlight beta (public link in Apple's beta review on 2026-10-24). No web client; no hosted cloud execution.
MCP: Yes: one MCP gateway per session (Realm's agent, terminal, browser, docs and workspace tools) that also proxies third-party MCP servers without handing the agent their credentials
Cost / token visibility: Partial: usage summaries, budgets and plan-limit readouts (usage.*, limits.get); depth not verified here
Model choice: Per agent; one picker across harnesses with effort and fast mode
Setup: Install the app (Mac dmg, Linux AppImage or deb, Windows installer); first run asks for an agent and a space name, sign-in optional, no Realm account. Headless: `<app>/resources/bin/realm serve`
Hands-on status (this box): v2.5.0 release, Linux AppImage on Xvfb: first window 3.32 s, 968 MB process tree, no account wall (Orca 1.4.230 on the same runner, same probe: 4.10 s, 922 MB). Driven end-to-end headless with the stub agent through the `realm` command the AppImage ships (`realm serve` + `realm run`, no Node, no display): 18/18 verified over 3 runs, 6 launched in 0.51 to 0.57 s, peak RSS 342 to 345 MB, server ready in 0.51 to 0.52 s (Orca on the same runner: 2.58 to 2.67 s, 1227 to 1347 MB, 3.24 to 3.34 s); crash isolation; merge 5/6. Run by Realm's author on a GitHub ubuntu-latest runner (runs/F-realm/environment.txt); earlier CI-build, container and macOS runs agree.
Known issues / caveats: The Linux and Windows builds are new (2.3); docs/platforms.md says what has run there (the Linux AppImage and deb on GitHub runners) and what has not. Found while measuring: the v2.5.0 Windows installer's server cannot load one of its packages (`pkce-challenge`) after install, so the installed Windows app does not start its server; the unpacked Windows build works, and a fix is being prepared. The iPhone app is a beta. README says 'in active development'.
Notes: Submitted by Realm's author, who also wrote the `realm` CLI, the remote runtime and the Linux packaging changes measured here. The numbers come from the published v2.5.0 release (2026-10-24), the first that ships `resources/bin/realm`, checked against the sha256 it records. GitHub figures fetched after the bench snapshot.
